I agree with you. Busan also reminds me of Rio de Janeiro a lot. Beach, mountains and Gamcheon Cultural Village is like Favela in Rio but is very safe and clean. It is absoultely amazing and hidden gem city.  You should have visited Huinnyeoul Cultural Village, which is reminiscent of Rio's Vigidal Favela. Like Gamcheon Cultural Village or Rio's Favela, this village was also created by people with nowhere else to go; however, it is built on a much steeper cliff than Vigidal Favela and is much closer to the beach, giving it a more dramatic feeling. If you happen to visit Busan again, I highly recommend visiting Hanyeoul Culture Village to compare the vibe with what you felt at Vigidal Favela.

Busan.....the best city in Korea? To us it is not, first, a lot of the real old buildings were scrapped, to be replaced with high-rise buildings, and what is considered to be old were fast-erected small houses because so many were homeless after the war and something had to be done about that. Yes, they are colorful, and there is art but not many kinds of lived-in Hanok villages. The ocean shoreline is riddled with shipping container storage areas, Just walk out the back of Central Station and there is a massive, wide road building sites for kilometers and hundreds of high-rise buildings in progress. The new future cruise liner dock is a huge building site mess that will still take several years before one can say: It's pretty here. Yes, the famous well-known beaches are nice and this is why there are so many masses of people there because elsewhere it just does not measure up to those outstanding beaches with artwork created out of sand, acrobatic show activities, cable cars, panorama tramways. In Seoul however, the city sparkles brightly in all directions - but again, this is only what we think and we are not really important. Whoever visits Busan now, there are now three tourist bus lines operational, just walk out from the central station and keep left, and there you see the taxis, and next to them are the busses. The Busan city traffic is horrifying, we understand the need for wider new roads. If one hires a cab - they have less road use priority than the busses, one might spend hours sitting in the back of a taxi only inching slowly forward while the tourist busses zoom forward to keep up the timetable plan posted at every bus stop.

So temple foods is a guaranteed 10/10 for vegan tourists visiting Korea.
